items.name: [QA] Non Secure Links to Stanford
items.note:
This Policy identifies links that start HTTP:// that also contain "stanford.edu"

All Stanford sites should be using SSL, so the link should be https and not http.

items.name: [A11y] Bad Alt Text
items.note: ALT text should not include the words "Picture of" or "Image of". Also, if the file extension is present it is probably a file name and not an ALT text.

items.name: [QA] Google Drive Folder

items.name: [A11y] ALT text is [object Object]

items.name: [A11y] Pages without Accessibility Link
items.note:
All Stanford sites, per university policy 6.8.1, should have a link on the page to information about accessibility and how to report a complaint.  

https://adminguide.stanford.edu/chapters/computing/digital-accessibility/accessibility-electronic-content

University websites are to contain a mechanism for users to report accessibility barriers to a designated person, with notification to the Office of Digital Accessibility. This may include an accessible online form, email, or other contact information to report the accessibility barrier. The recommended location for this information is on the website's "Accessibility" page, and to provide a link to that page in the header or footer that persists on every page.

Pages in this report lack a link to the Stanford Accessibility Policy. https://www.stanford.edu/site/accessibility

items.name: [A11y] Accessibility Overlay Present
items.note: Accessibility overlays, such as AccessiBe, UserWay, etc. harms the accessibility of a page more than it helps. It should not be used on any Stanford website.

items.name: [A11y][QA] Printed URLs & Email Addresses
items.note: Link where the link text is a URL such as: www.stanford.edu

items.name: Large pages with multiple referrals
items.note:
Find large pages that are linked to more than twice across your site. 

Large pages take longer to load, which can have a negative impact on user experience. 

If a page has multiple referrals, it’s likely to get a lot of traffic. Reducing the size of such pages can significantly speed up load time for site visitors.

items.name: [SEO][QA] Large Pictures (Dimensions of 2000+ wide or 1000+ tall)
items.note: Find any picture that has a width greater than 2000 pixels or high greater than 1000 pixels.

items.name: [A11y] Words in all capital letters
items.note:
Avoid unnecessary use of capitals. Using all capital letters can make it harder to read, and it can also appear that you are shouting at the reader. This is recommended by several dyslexia organizations including the British Dyslexia Association. You can find a Dyslexia Friendly Style Guide on the [British Dyslexia Associations website](http://www.bdadyslexia.org.uk/common/ckeditor/filemanager/userfiles/About_Us/policies/Dyslexia_Style_Guide.pdf). Only matching text that is originally all capitals in the HTML, not after applying css. Words separated by `
` are not considered consecutive.

items.name: [QA] Images larger than 1MB
items.note: Images larger than 1mb are problematic for all users, especially on mobile devices.

items.name: [A11y][SEO] Long paragraphs
items.note: Highlights paragraphs longer than 600 characters. For online texts, the recommended length of a paragraph is 40-50 words, or four to five lines. Keeping your paragraphs short helps boost comprehension and keeps your reader’s focus.

items.name: [QA] Find repeated, short words
items.note:
Find words of 5 characters or less that are repeated directly after each other. 
Many repeated words are likely small words that are repeated by mistake, often caused by editing the text, more so than actually writing down the words.
This policy only looks for words in lower case.

items.name: [A11y] Captions: YouTube Embeds (Videos)
items.note: Locates all videos embedded from YouTube. Use this report to locate and confirm that all of these videos should have accurate captions.

items.name: [A11y][QA] Email addresses that are not a link (with valid mailto).
items.note:
Find all email addresses that do not have the 'mailto:' attribute.

It is not good practice to have an email address that is not clickable. This will require the user to copy the email address in order to send an email.

items.name: "Lorem Ipsum" placeholder text
items.note: Find pages with the text 'Lorem Ipsum', which is often used as a placeholder text when creating new pages.

items.name: [A11y][SEO] Vague Link Text
items.note:
The text in your links should clear to users where they are going when activating the link. Vague link text such as "click here" does not provide any information to the user about where they are going. This is important for users of Screen Reading software as they may only see a list of links with several "click here" and not know what each does. 

This is also important for SEO purposes, as google puts weight on the text of your link for helping understanding the purpose of the destination page.

items.name: High-level pages with broken links
items.note:
Find pages at level 1 and 2 that contain one or more broken links. This typically includes your home page and other main pages. 

This Policy looks for "confirmed" broken links: URLs that return error codes 404 (page not found) or 410 (gone).

items.name: Homepages missing image alt text
items.note:
Find homepages (level 1 pages) that have images missing a text alternative.

In order to be fully accessible to all visitors, images need to have a text alternative added to the code (HTML).
Read about Accessibility & Image Alt text best practices in our Help Center

items.name: [QA] Homepages (High-level pages) with broken links
items.note: Find pages at level 1 that contain one or more broken links. This Policy looks for "confirmed" broken links: URLs that return error codes 404 (page not found) or 410 (gone).

items.name: [QA] LInks to Unsafe domains
items.note:
Find all links to unsafe domains on your site(s) as defined by Google.
Unsafe domains can affect your reputation and direct visitors to harmful sites.

items.name: [A11y][SEO] Images missing an alt attribute
items.note:
Find all images on your site(s) with no alt attribute.
There are several reasons to always remember alt attributes on your images.
It will provide text for visitors who can’t see images in their browsers or visitors using a screen reader.
Using Alt attributes on images will also improve your website's placement in search engine result pages.

items.name: A11y: Headers exceeding 250 characters
items.note:
If your heading is longer than 250 characters, its probably not a heading, but a paragraph that has been formatted to "look big". 

Find pages that use headers over a certain length to avoid line breaks that might misalign with the website layout.
This is a configurable template to accommodate different header styles.

items.note:

items.name: [QA] Wrong time format (Time not seperated with : but with another character)
items.note: Looks for time formats that do not conform to your chosen standard. You can choose from two formats: 24-hour notation: where the units of time are separated by a colon, e.g. 23:59:00, or 12-hour notation: where the units of time are separated by a colon, followed by “am” or “pm”, e.g. 3:45 am. Using the same time format throughout will give your website a unified presentation.
